frequency_question: How often does a congressional joint resolution blocking a submitted 123 agreement successfully pass both chambers and survive or override a presidential veto?
membership_rule: Includes all formal 123 agreements transmitted to Congress for the statutory review period; excludes informal consultations or agreements that were withdrawn prior to formal submission.
window: The statutory congressional review period (typically 90 continuous session days) following submission.
provenance_note: claims 40 cases from only 3 named (13.3x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: Over 40 agreements submitted historically across multiple decades; zero instances of successful legislative blocking via joint resolution.
known_gaps: Some minor amendments or peaceful nuclear cooperation extensions might be bundled, but major 123 agreements are fully accounted for.
skeleton: Total historical 123 agreements submitted for congressional review since the modern framework was established, partitioned by whether a resolution of disapproval was introduced, passed, and enacted.
multiplier: Approximately 40 total agreements submitted historically, zero of which have successfully been blocked by a joint resolution of disapproval overriding or avoiding a veto.
validity_reason: The statutory framework of the Atomic Energy Act governing 123 agreements has remained stable for decades and is unlikely to change structurally before this date.
